# Development Optimization Passes List

<!-- Don't bother formatting this. -->
<!-- mdformat global-off -->

This is an automatically generated list of all internal xls developtment
optimization passes available with the default `opt_main`. Normal optimization
passes may be found
[here](https://google.github.io/xls/passes_list/).
This is generated automatically based on comments in the header files.

!!! WARNING
    These passes are mostly intended for debugging and development use cases by
    the XLS development team and allow for the manipulation of ir files in ways
    that may not be desirable for general optimization use.

If the opt level is set below 'Min opt level' the pass will act as a no-op.

If the opt level is set above 'Cap opt level' the pass (or passes within the
compound pass) will be executed with the opt level capped to the specified
value.

!!! WARNING
    Many of these passes have descriptions generated by the Gemini LLM and may
    not accurately reflect the behavior of the passes. As time goes on manual
    verification or editing of the pass descriptions may be done to improve
    accuracy.

## decompose_dataflow - Decompose dataflow {#decompose_dataflow}


Decompose and flatten all compound data type dataflow. This replaces all
array and tuple operations with operations on base values except directly
around externally visible values.

This pass is meant for testing and measurement.


[Header](http://github.com/google/xls/tree/main/xls/dev_tools/dev_passes/decompose_dataflow_pass.h)






## literalize_zero_bits - Literalize zero bits {#literalize_zero_bits}


!!! NOTE
    What follows was generated by the Gemini LLM. Not human verified.

`LiteralizeZeroBits` (`literalize_zero_bits`) replaces all non-literal,
non-parameter operations that produce a zero-width bit vector (`bits[0]`)
with a constant `bits[0]` literal (`value=0`).

Because a `bits[0]` type carries zero bits of runtime information, any pure
computation producing `bits[0]` always evaluates to the unique zero-bit
value. Replacing such nodes with a `Literal` of `UBits(0, 0)` severs data
dependencies on their operands, simplifying the IR graph and allowing dead
code elimination to remove upstream logic that only feeds zero-width values.

### How It Works

The pass iterates over all nodes in the `FunctionBase` and checks whether
each node `n` satisfies:
* `n->GetType()->IsBits()` with `bit_count() == 0`,
* `!n->Is<Literal>()` (already a literal), and
* `!n->Is<Param>()` (parameters are preserved so the function signature and
  parameter list remain valid).

Every matching node has its uses replaced with a new `Literal` node holding
`Value(UBits(0, 0))`.

### Example

```
// Before
fn f(x: bits[8]) -> bits[8] {
  empty_slice: bits[0] = bit_slice(x, start=0, width=0)
  ret result: bits[8] = concat(empty_slice, x)
}
```

After `LiteralizeZeroBits`:

```
// After
fn f(x: bits[8]) -> bits[8] {
  lit_zero_bits: bits[0] = literal(value=0)
  ret result: bits[8] = concat(lit_zero_bits, x)
}
```


[Header](http://github.com/google/xls/tree/main/xls/dev_tools/dev_passes/literalize_zero_bits_pass.h)






## proc_state_legalization_shim - Proc State Legalization Pass {#proc_state_legalization_shim}


Compatibility shim to use the scheduling pass 'ProcStateLegalizationPass' in
the optimization pass pipeline for modernizing procs.

!!! NOTE
    What follows was generated by the Gemini LLM. Not human verified.

`ProcStateLegalizationPassShim` (`proc_state_legalization_shim`) is an
`OptimizationPass` wrapper around the scheduling pass
`ProcStateLegalizationPass`. Because `ProcStateLegalizationPass` inherits
from `SchedulingFunctionBasePass` and normally executes inside the scheduling
pipeline, this shim constructs a package-wide `SchedulingContext`
(`SchedulingContext::CreateForWholePackage`) and default
`SchedulingPassOptions` so proc state legalization can be invoked directly
from `opt_main` and optimization pass pipelines when modernizing or testing
procs.

### What the Wrapped `ProcStateLegalizationPass` Does

For each `Proc` in the package (non-proc `FunctionBase`s are skipped),
`ProcStateLegalizationPass` legalizes every `StateElement` in three steps:

1. **Mutual Exclusion Assertions (`AddMutualExclusionAsserts`)**:
   * **Write Mutual Exclusion (`AddNextValueMutualExclusionAssert`)**: If a
     state element has two or more `next_value` (`Next`) nodes, concatenates
     all of their predicates (`__<state>__next_value_predicates`), applies
     `one_hot(..., lsb_prio=true)` and slices off the MSB, compares equality
     with the concatenated predicates (`__<state>__at_most_one_next_value`),
     and emits an `assert` labeled
     `__<state>__at_most_one_next_value_assert` verifying that at most one
     `next_value` fires in any activation.
   * **Read Mutual Exclusion (`AddStateReadMutualExclusionAssert`)**: If a
     state element has two or more `state_read` nodes, similarly concatenates
     their predicates (substituting `literal(1)` for any unpredicated read)
     and emits an `assert` labeled `__<state>__at_most_one_read_assert`
     verifying that at most one `state_read` is active at a time.

2. **Write-Without-Read Assertions (`AddWriteWithoutReadAsserts`)**:
   If a state element has one or more `next_value` nodes and all of its
   `state_read` nodes are predicated, computes the disjunction of all read
   predicates (`__<state>__state_read_predicates_nary_or`). For each
   `next_value` node, emits an `assert` labeled
   `__<state>__next_<id>_without_read_assert` checking
   `any_read_active | !next_predicate`, ensuring a state update never fires
   when the state read is disabled.

3. **Default `next_value` Generation (`AddDefaultNextValues`)**:
   Ensures every state element has an explicit state update under all
   conditions:
   * If any `next_value` is unconditional, or if an existing no-op
     `next_value` (`IsNoOpNext`) already guards `nor(other_predicates)` (so
     the pass is idempotent), no default is added. (When run in the
     scheduling pipeline with `default_next_value_z3_rlimit` set, a solver
     can also prove the predicates exhaustive; the shim uses default
     `SchedulingPassOptions` where this limit is unset.)
   * If no `next_value` nodes exist for the state element, emits a default
     `next_value(param=state, value=state_read, predicate=read_pred)` for
     each `state_read`.
   * Otherwise, computes `__<state>__no_explicit_next_active =
     nor(predicates...)` and, for each `state_read`, adds a default
     `next_value` holding the state unchanged (`value=state_read`) when
     `no_explicit_next_active` (ANDed with `state_read->predicate()`, if
     present) is true.

### Example

```
// Before
proc counter(st: bits[32], init={0}) {
  en: bits[1] = ...
  inc: bits[32] = add(st, literal(value=1))
  next_inc: () = next_value(param=st, value=inc, predicate=en)
}
```

After `ProcStateLegalizationPassShim`, an explicit default `next_value` is
added to retain `st` when `en` is false:

```
// After
proc counter(st: bits[32], init={0}) {
  en: bits[1] = ...
  inc: bits[32] = add(st, literal(value=1))
  next_inc: () = next_value(param=st, value=inc, predicate=en)
  __st__no_explicit_next_active: bits[1] = not(en)
  st_default_st: () = next_value(
      param=st, value=st, predicate=__st__no_explicit_next_active)
}
```


[Header](http://github.com/google/xls/tree/main/xls/dev_tools/dev_passes/proc_state_legalization_pass_shim.h)






## remove_identifiers_unsafe - UNSAFE: Remove all identifiers {#remove_identifiers_unsafe}


A pass version of 'remove_identifers_main'. Running this pass will rewrite
the package to remove the names of all functions, procs, nodes, channels,
etc.

This should only be used while investigating optimizer behavior using the
ir-visualizer or other tools.

!!! WARNING
    This pass does not preserve externally visible names. Once run on a design
    the various io-constraint and other configs which rely on naming pieces of
    the design will not work. This pass is only for dev/ investigatory purposes.

!!! NOTE
    This pass **does not** preserve the id number of nodes.


[Header](http://github.com/google/xls/tree/main/xls/dev_tools/dev_passes/remove_identifiers_pass.h)






## remove_one_hot_sel - One Hot Select Removal Pass {#remove_one_hot_sel}


Pass which replaces OneHotSelects with equivalent Selects without regard to
profitability concerns. This pass is meant for investigation and analysis use
only and should not be used for normal optimization pipelines.

To avoid extreme proliferation of nodes, we only translate OneHotSelects with
a selector bitwidth <= 16.


[Header](http://github.com/google/xls/tree/main/xls/dev_tools/dev_passes/remove_one_hot_select_pass.h)






## to_zero_ext - DebugPass: To ZeroExt Pass {#to_zero_ext}


Converts any canonicalized zero-exts back from concat(zero, ...) to zero_ext
since it generally makes for easier to read/visualize graphs. This pass
is not meant to be used as an optimization pass at all.


[Header](http://github.com/google/xls/tree/main/xls/dev_tools/dev_passes/to_zero_ext_pass.h)
